s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis in the axilla
salient_findings: Asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with brownish peripheral border
Nonindurated and well-defined annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Vascular proliferation with small, dilated, and irregular vascular channels
key_facts: 5-year history of gradually enlarging plaque
No previous history of trauma
No systemic symptoms
Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Plaque is nonindurated and well-defined
No local lymphadenopathy
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests are negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis

shortlist.label: Dabska Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with immunohistochemical findings of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40

shortlist.label: Verrucous Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible consideration given the plaque's appearance and location, although less likely than Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma

shortlist.label: Hobnail Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of a reddish-brown plaque, but less typical location and morphology

shortlist.label: Papillary Intralymphatic Angioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Remains a possibility due to the vascular nature of the lesion and the presence of ecchymosis, despite being less common

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border, combined with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation and prominent hemosiderin deposits, is consistent with Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.

rejected.label: Dabska Tumor
rejected.why: Dabska tumor typically presents with more aggressive features and higher proliferation rates, which is not consistent with the low Ki-67 index in this case.

rejected.label: Verrucous Hemangioma
rejected.why: Verrucous hemangioma usually has a more verrucous or wart-like appearance, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hobnail Hemangioma
rejected.why: Hobnail hemangioma typically has a more distinctive hobnail-like appearance of the endothelial cells, which is not mentioned in the histologic findings.

rejected.label: Papillary Intralymphatic Angioendothelioma
rejected.why: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma is a rare tumor that typically presents with more complex vascular architecture and is often associated with lymphatic vessels, which is not the primary feature in this case.
